title: State of Libya
capsule: Libya's post-2014 polity—formally the State of Libya under the Tobruk-based House of Representatives and internationally recognised Government of National Accord and its successor Government of National Unity—emerged from the collapse of authority following the 2011 civil war that ousted and killed Muammar Gaddafi. The country remained split between rival administrations based in Tobruk/Benghazi in the east, backed by General Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army, and governments successively seated in Tripoli in the west; a UN-brokered Government of National Unity under Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh was formed in early 2021 but failed to hold unified elections by the end of 2021. The period saw significant involvement by foreign powers including the UAE, Egypt, Turkey, Russia, and Wagner Group mercenaries, turning Libyan territory into a proxy battleground. By 2025 the country remained formally unified under a contested central bank and Government of National Unity but de facto divided.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial control during this period was highly fluid and contested; mapping any single authority's extent to a fixed polygon is a significant simplification of a complex, shifting conflict landscape.
